CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports left arm pain that began approximately two weeks ago. He woke around 2 AM with severe pain, applied ice which provided some relief. The pain started in the hand and radiates down the entire arm. He experienced similar episodes on multiple nights over a week. He was evaluated by another physician who suspected a pinched nerve. He was prescribed numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin. Since starting these medications, nighttime symptoms have improved though hand symptoms persist. He reports hand weakness with gripping and notes a previous finger injury that does not work properly. Symptoms have been flaring for the last week, though neck pain has not bothered him the last couple of nights.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies neck pain with head turning or shoulder movement. Reports mild strain with head turning. Reports hand weakness with gripping. Reports neuropathy affecting lower extremities from knees to feet.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Neuropathy (knees to feet, VA-related disability 1%)
Cervical arthritis
Previous finger injury
Previous lower back MRI

MEDICATIONS
Numbing medicine
Neck pill
Gabapentin (dose uncertain, approximately 300-100 mg)
Eliquis

ALLERGIES
Not discussed

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed

SOCIAL HISTORY
Veteran with VA disability
Lives with lady friend who assists with medication management
Uses wheelchair for mobility

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Elderly white male in wheelchair, no apparent distress. Neurologic: 1+ bilateral biceps and triceps brachioradialis reflexes, all negative bilaterally. Gait not assessed. Upper and lower extremity strength and sensation per template. Musculoskeletal: Non-tender over cervical spine, mildly restricted cervical extension, symmetric right and left lateral rotation with mild lateral neck pain but no radicular pain, Spurling's maneuver benign. Bilateral hand grip strength intact. Sensation symmetric bilaterally.

RESULTS
Cervical x-ray: Significant disc degeneration at C5-6 and to a lower extent at C4-5 and C3-4. Significant lower lumbar facet arthropathy at C6-7. C7-T1 difficult to visualize on current x-rays.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy, possible contribution of peripheral neuropathy
2. Neck pain in the setting of arthritis and disc degeneration

Plan: Obtain cervical MRI to determine exact location of nerve root compression. Tentatively schedule left C7-T1 epidural injection (exact location pending MRI results). Continue home exercise program. Continue gabapentin twice daily. Patient denies blood thinner use. Follow up after epidural to assess symptom relief.
